title: Remove a staple without tearing the papers
instruction: Remove the staple without tearing the papers, then lay the two sheets separately.
context: Preparing documents for scanning requires releasing a clinched fastener while preserving thin paper around its holes.
setup: Proposed fixed setup: two white 80 gsm paper sheets, each 210 × 148 × 0.1 mm, on a 210 × 128 × 20 mm rigid document support. Sheet centres are (0.32, 0) and (0.32, 0.012) m; their far edges overhang by 20 and 32 mm. A steel staple has a 12.8 mm crown, 6 mm legs and 0.50 × 0.30 mm wire section, clinched through both sheets at x=0.227, y=-0.050 m. A 108 × 18 × 16 mm steel/ABS forked lever remover rests at x=0.28, y=-0.20 m. The 747.5 mm-high table and every detailed placement are in setup.json. Native settling precedes control; no sheet pins or fixed staple. Full-scene setup and screenshot are unvalidated.
scoring: 0.5 when at least one staple leg is entirely clear of both sheets. 1.0 when both legs are clear and the sheets lie separately with at least 30 mm between their nearest edges, released for three seconds. Any tear extending over 2 mm beyond an original hole, new damage elsewhere, broken staple, altered sheets or invalid evidence gives zero. All other outcomes score zero.
run_limit: Proposed 2,400 control steps (120 seconds at 20 Hz); no robot run yet.
reset_notes: Use fresh matched paper and one fresh staple for every trial. Record both sides before and after. Reuse the remover only while intact.
fidelity: Native steel contact produces permanent plastic bending; a no-contact control stays unchanged and halving the time step changes residual bend by 0.28%. Real 0.1 mm surface-FEM sheets have explicit puncture holes. Excess membrane/bending strain or wire crossing intact triangles irreversibly invalidates the trial; no post-tear topology is rendered. Paper is isotropic and steel bending is currently planar. The full free-staple scene and ordinary robot extraction remain unvalidated.
scores: Not run. No demo, Dream score or media exists. This is not submission metadata.
